summary: We made an audio based guessing game using greenhouse gas data. Players are given an audio clip and asked to match it using sliders. These controls correspond to CO2, methane, and NO2, and overlay data onto a world map. The closer your guess, the lower your score.
details:
• Interface
    • The CO2 slider controls the amplitude of a sawtooth wave.
    • The Methane slider controls the amplitude of another sawtooth wave.
    • The NO2 slider controls the amplitude of another sawtooth wave.
  • Tools we used
    • Javascript and html
    • Leafletjs https://leafletjs.com/
    • Tonejs https://tonejs.github.io/
  • Motivation (info from [1] and [2])
    • Methane, carbon dioxide, and nitrous oxide all significantly contribute to global warming.
    • Global Warming Potential (GWP) is a measure of the energy emission of a ton of gas compared to that of CO2, it is a measure of the relative effects of different pollutants. GWP for CO2 is 1, GWP for CH4 is ~30, and GWP for NO2 is 273.
    • The metric tons emitted per year emitted for CO2 is 6343, for CH4 is 883, and for NO2 is 485.
    • The approx. weight of all humans in the US is 27 million metric tons.
  • Data we used
    • Methane
      • https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov/datasets/GFEI_CH4_1/summary?keywords=l3methane%5C
    • CO2
      • https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov/datasets/OCO2_GEOS_L3CO2_DAY_10r/summary?keywords=l3co2
      • Data from orbiting carbon observatory 2 Goddard earth observing system launched July 2, 2014
    • NO2
      • https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov/datasets/SFC_NITROGEN_DIOXIDE_CONC_1/summary?keywords=l3nitrogen
      • Data from the ozone monitoring instrument, part of NASA’s Aura mission launched in 2004
  • Future work
    • Curate locations of interest to highlight pollution data in various ecological zones such as urban centers.
    • Illustrate time evolution of pollution data.
    • Include sliders for other pollutants too.
    • Add game mechanics for speed based challenges and historical data.
    • Include additional facts about greenhouse gas data at locations and times.

    • [2] https://www.epa.gov/ghgemissions/overview-greenhouse-gases

NO2 Data Source: Nitrogen Dioxide Surface-Level Annual Average Concentrations V1 (SFC_NITROGEN_DIOXIDE_CONC)
Methane Data Source: Global Inventory of Methane Emissions from Fuel Exploitation (GFEI_CH4)
